Diphthong before a vowel shortened, ὦ πόποι [O alas!], or
Ἐπάθομεν πάθος δυσαχές, ὦ πόποι [We suffered a grievous suffering, O alas!],
with hiatus in fine dochmii [at the end of the dochmius].

thus Markland for φρεσίν [for the mind]. πορόντας [providing] for περῶντας [crossing] restored Hermann, and the scholiast, who explains by διδόντας [giving].

Προστετριμμένον τε πρὸς ἄλλοισιν οἴκοις καὶ [And rubbed against other houses and]
he goes having a deceitful eye
the strength of the traveling torch
to destroy the ancestral city and the native gods
but we ourselves are destroyed from within by our own hands
you said that we are utterly destroyed
when goods are being destroyed from the house
and after how long has the city been destroyed?
do you think Troy has now been destroyed?
your foot, O king, destroyer of Ilium
and the murderers of their father, destroyers of the house
having met my father at the swift-crossing passage of sorrows
having crossed the strait of Athamantian Helle
with devices he yoked the strait of Helle
he crosses the strait of Helle
the headland overlooking the Saronic strait
